method: agent-browser (Chromium 152 headless) at 1440x900 and 390x844; verified in-browser form submits, theme toggles, dead CTAs; static source review of every page.tsx and the Nav/Footer/ThemeProvider

summary.horizontal_scroll_observed: none — all 14 pages pass at 1440x900 and iPhone-14 (390x844)
summary.brand_consistency: OK: 'Nexora' is absent from src/, README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md. Body text on /contact, /help, /status, /nonexistent does NOT include the word 'Nexa' (no Logo/Nav/Footer rendered).

grep_evidence.nexora: rg -n Nexora returned 0 matches in src/ README.md CONTRIBUTING.md (excluding 'Nexa Pay').

setTimeout_stubs.src/app/signup/page.tsx:35: setTimeout(() => { setSubmitting(false); toast.success("Account created — check your email"); }, 400);

issues.title: Signup form is a fake setTimeout stub — no real account creation
issues.description: onSubmit runs client-side validation then `setTimeout(() => { setSubmitting(false); toast.success('Account created — check your email'); }, 400)`. There is no fetch to /api/v1/*, no cookie set, no redirect. Verified in-browser: filling the form and clicking 'Create account' shows the success toast while the URL stays on /signup and document.cookie is empty. For a fintech handling money this is a trust and security disaster — a user believes an account exists that doesn't.
issues.fix: Wire onSubmit to a real auth endpoint (e.g. POST /api/v1/auth/signup) that creates the user, sends an email, and redirects to /login or a 'verify your email' page. On error, show toast.error and stay on page. Until the backend exists, hide the form or display a 'coming soon' state — do not fake success.

issues.title: Login form is a fake setTimeout stub — no real authentication
issues.description: Same pattern as signup: `setTimeout(() => { setSubmitting(false); toast.success('Welcome back'); }, 400)`. Verified in-browser: 'Welcome back' toast appears, URL stays on /login, document.cookie is empty, no session is created. Anyone can 'sign in' with any email/password combination. Combined with the dashboard having no auth gate, this is a full authentication bypass.
issues.fix: Call a real /api/v1/auth/login endpoint, set an httpOnly session cookie, and redirect to /dashboard on success. Show toast.error on 401/403. Add middleware or layout-level session check to /dashboard so it redirects to /login when unauthenticated.

issues.title: ThemeProvider is not in the root layout — half the app is stuck in dark mode
issues.description: RootLayout renders `<html lang="en" suppressHydrationWarning className="dark">` and never wraps children in <ThemeProvider>. Only /, /terms, /privacy, /kyc add <ThemeProvider> per-page. The other 10 routes (/signup, /login, /dashboard, /docs, /contact, /help, /status, /security, /cookies, /nonexistent) have no ThemeProvider context. Because ThemeToggle uses `useTheme()` which throws outside a provider, those pages can never render a working toggle, and `document.documentElement.className` stays 'dark' regardless of user preference (verified: localStorage ps-theme='dark' is set on / but ignored on /signup).
issues.fix: Move <ThemeProvider> into src/app/layout.tsx so it wraps {children} once at the root. Remove the per-page <ThemeProvider> wrappers from page.tsx, terms/page.tsx, privacy/page.tsx, kyc/page.tsx. Drop `className="dark"` from <html> — let the provider manage the class after hydration.

issues.title: Footer newsletter form is a dead submit — no handler, no API
issues.description: The footer renders `<form>` with an email input and a submit button but no onSubmit handler, no action attribute (verified: form.action resolves to the current URL), and no API route. Pressing Enter or clicking Subscribe navigates to the same page via GET with the email in the query string and silently drops the subscriber. The form appears on every page that renders <Footer> — /, /terms, /privacy, /kyc — so this is a 4-route-wide leak of marketing intent.
issues.fix: Add an onSubmit handler that POSTs to /api/v1/newsletter (or a third-party like ConvertKit/Buttondown), disables the button, and shows a sonner toast on success/error. Or replace with a real Link to a signup page that captures email as a query param.

issues.title: Footer social icons are dead `href="#"` links
issues.description: Four social icons (Twitter, Instagram, Youtube, Facebook) all use `<a href="#" aria-label="social link">`. Clicking jumps to the top of the page instead of opening the brand's social profile. For a fintech where trust signals matter, dead social links read as 'this company doesn't actually exist'.
issues.fix: Replace `#` with the real brand social URLs (twitter.com/nexapay, instagram.com/nexapay, etc.) and set target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer". If the accounts don't exist yet, remove the icons until they do.

issues.title: KYC form ships with an empty DEMO_API_KEY — every submission 401s
issues.description: Line 24: `const DEMO_API_KEY = "";` then line 59: `Authorization: \`Bearer ${DEMO_API_KEY}\``. The /api/v1/kyc/verify-bvn route enforces API-key auth, so it returns 401 'Invalid or missing API key'. Verified in-browser: filling BVN+ID and clicking 'Verify BVN' shows 'Verification failed: Invalid or missing API key. Send Authorization: Bearer nxp_test_...'. A real user landing on /kyc cannot verify their identity. The comment claims this is the same key as the Endpoint Explorer, but it's empty.
issues.fix: Either ship a public demo key whose tier is restricted to KYC verify (and rotate it regularly), or proxy the KYC submit through a server action that injects the secret key server-side. The empty-string constant should be removed.

issues.title: Pricing 'Talk to sales' CTA points to /signup
issues.description: The Business tier card has `cta: 'Talk to sales'` but the Link is hardcoded to `href="/signup"` (same as Personal and Plus). A prospect wanting to talk to sales is dumped into the consumer self-serve signup flow — they will bounce. Sales-cycle revenue is lost.
issues.fix: Add a `ctaHref` field per tier in TIERS: Personal/Plus → '/signup', Business → '/contact'. Render `<Link href={t.ctaHref}>`. Consider pre-filling the contact form subject via query string.

issues.title: Dashboard top-bar buttons (Search / Notifications / Settings) are dead
issues.description: Three icon buttons in the dashboard header — Search, Notifications, Settings — have `aria-label` set but no onClick handler (verified: b.onclick === null for all three, click produces no dialog, no toast, no navigation). They are also `type="submit"`, which would submit any enclosing form (they are not in one today, but the attribute is a latent bug). The notification bell even has a red dot suggesting unread notifications — pure decoration.
issues.fix: Either wire each button to a real action (open a command palette, show a notifications dropdown, route to /dashboard/settings) or remove the buttons until the features exist. Change `type` to `type="button"` to be safe.

issues.title: /contact, /help, /status, /security, /cookies are stranded pages — no Nav, no Footer, no Logo
issues.description:
These 5 legal/support pages render only `
…
` with no Nav, no Footer, no Logo, and (except /help) no internal links. Verified: /contact, /status, /security, /cookies have zero elements pointing to other Nexa Pay routes. A user who lands on /status from a Google search has no way to sign up, log in, or return to marketing without editing the URL or pressing Back. Body text on /contact, /help, /status doesn't even contain the word 'Nexa' — the brand mark is invisible.
issues.fix: Wrap each of these pages in the same <Nav> + <Footer> shell used by /terms and /privacy. Alternatively, move the chrome into RootLayout so every route inherits it. Add at minimum a 'Back to home' link and the Logo to each page.

issues.title: /nonexistent (404) page has no brand and no ThemeProvider
issues.description: The 404 page renders '404 / Page not found / Back to home' but does not include the Nexa Pay Logo, the brand name, Nav, or Footer (verified: body text contains 'Nexa' = false). It is also 'use client' with framer-motion but lacks <ThemeProvider>, so the page cannot inherit any user theme preference and stays in whatever className the root html was hardcoded to. Title is also the homepage default 'Nexa Pay — One switch for every payment.' instead of 'Page not found — Nexa Pay'.
issues.fix: Render the Logo and a 'Back to home' Button at minimum; add `export const metadata = { title: 'Page not found — Nexa Pay' }` (or use generateMetadata). Move ThemeProvider to root layout so this page inherits theme. Render <Nav> + <Footer> for consistency.

issues.title: Page titles are the homepage default on 6 routes — bad for tabs, history, and SEO
issues.file: src/app/signup/page.tsx, src/app/login/page.tsx, src/app/dashboard/page.tsx, src/app/docs/page.tsx, src/app/kyc/page.tsx, src/app/not-found.tsx
issues.description: Verified via document.title: /signup, /login, /dashboard, /docs, /kyc, and /nonexistent all show 'Nexa Pay — One switch for every payment.' (the default from layout.tsx). Only /terms, /privacy, /contact, /help, /status, /security, /cookies set their own `export const metadata`. Browser tabs are indistinguishable, history menu is useless, and SEO is weakened on critical conversion pages (signup, login).
issues.fix: Add `export const metadata: Metadata = { title: 'Sign up — Nexa Pay', description: '…' }` to each of the 6 pages. For 'use client' pages (signup, login, dashboard, docs, not-found) split the page into a server wrapper that exports metadata + a client component for the interactive body, or use generateMetadata.

issues.title: Footer 'All systems operational' is a hardcoded lie
issues.description: Line 110-113: a green pulsing dot + 'All systems operational' is rendered unconditionally on every page with a Footer. The /status page actually polls /api/health, but the Footer does not. If the API is down (or the database is degraded), the Footer continues to display 'All systems operational' — a misleading signal on a fintech where status matters. There is no fallback to 'Degraded' or 'Down'.
issues.fix: Make the Footer a small client component that fetches /api/health on mount (and on visibilitychange) and renders the dot color based on the real status. Or remove the status indicator from the Footer and link to /status instead.

issues.title: /status page hardcodes http://localhost:3000 for the health check
issues.description: Line 7: `await fetch('http://localhost:3000/api/health', { cache: 'no-store' })`. In any non-dev environment (Vercel, Docker container, k8s pod) this either resolves to the wrong host or fails entirely, returning `{status:'down', db:'down'}` and showing a red 'Degraded performance' banner even when the app is fine. The page is also `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` so this runs on every request.
issues.fix: Use a relative URL: `fetch('/api/health', { cache: 'no-store' })` — Next.js will resolve it to the current origin during SSR. Or use `headers()` to read the host and build an absolute URL. Remove the literal `http://localhost:3000`.

issues.title: Login 'Forgot?' link points to /signup
issues.description: Line 76-81: the 'Forgot?' password-reset link in the login form is `<Link href="/signup">`. A user who forgot their password is sent to the account-creation flow, not a password reset flow. This is confusing and signals the auth surface is incomplete.
issues.fix: Add a /reset-password page (or /forgot-password) and point the link there. Until that exists, point to /contact with a query like `?subject=Password reset` or hide the 'Forgot?' link entirely.

issues.title: /docs page has no signup/login CTA — developers can't convert
issues.description: The API reference page (the highest-intent developer page) only links back to '/' via the header arrow and the 'Back to home' footer link. There is no 'Get an API key' or 'Sign up' button. A developer who reads the docs and wants to try the API has to manually navigate to /signup. The footer text 'Need help? Back to home' is the only CTA — and it goes the wrong way.
issues.fix: Add a primary CTA in the docs header (e.g. 'Get an API key' → /signup) and a sidebar TOC of endpoint categories. Link the 'Need help?' line to /contact instead of /.

issues.title: Signup and login forms default to method="get" — passwords would land in the URL
issues.description: Neither form sets `method` on the <form> element (verified in-browser: form.method === 'get'). If JavaScript fails to load (network blip, ad blocker, CSP issue) the React onSubmit never runs and the browser falls back to native form submission — a GET to the current URL with `?password=…&email=…` in the query string. Passwords in URLs end up in browser history, server logs, and Referer headers. The actual JS handler also uses 'Account created' even though no account is created (see critical issue above).
issues.fix: Add `method="post"` and `action="/api/v1/auth/signup"` (or `/login`) to each form so the native fallback is a POST, not a GET. Even better, set `autoComplete` correctly (already done) and ensure the server route returns a redirect on success.

issues.title: Footer 'About us', 'Careers', 'Press', 'Community' all point to /contact
issues.description: In the COLS Company and Resources groups, four distinct links ('About us', 'Careers', 'Press', 'Community') all use `href: '/contact'`. A user who clicks 'Careers' expecting a jobs page lands on the generic contact form. This is a minor trust signal — it suggests the company is fronting placeholder links — but on a fintech it accumulates.
issues.fix: Either build out /about, /careers, /press pages or remove the placeholders and replace with a single 'Learn more about Nexa Pay → /contact' link. Don't ship four dead links to the same URL.

issues.title: ThemeProvider initial state flashes dark before reading localStorage
issues.description: useState('dark') is the initial render, and getInitialTheme() runs in a useEffect with queueMicrotask. Combined with `<html className="dark">` in layout.tsx, every first paint is dark — even if the user previously chose light (and the time-based auto says light). The class swap happens after hydration, producing a visible flash for light-mode users on every page load.
issues.fix: Add an inline script in <head> (before paint) that reads localStorage('ps-theme') and sets document.documentElement.classList before React hydrates. Pattern is the same as next-themes. Then set useState to 'dark' only as a server-rendered default.

issues.title: Dashboard sidebar nav items have no real destination
issues.description: The 8-item sidebar (Overview, Cards, Foreign, Crypto, eSIM, Bills, Business, Savings) is purely `onClick={() => setActive(t.id)}` — clicking changes the active highlight but the main panel keeps rendering the same <AppDemo> regardless of selection. A user clicking 'Cards' expects a cards view, not the same overview with a highlighted sidebar item. The active state is purely cosmetic.
issues.fix: Either route each sidebar item to a distinct URL segment (/dashboard/cards, /dashboard/foreign, etc.) with its own content, or render different content in the main panel based on `active`. At minimum, disable the inactive items or add a tooltip 'coming soon'.

issues.title: Nav anchor links (#features, #cards, #pricing) break on non-home pages
issues.description: The Nav and Footer emit links like `/#features`, `/#foreign`, `/#cards`, `/#crypto`, `/#business`, `/#pricing`, `/#app-demo`, `/#developers`. On /, these scroll to the section. But on /terms, /privacy, /kyc (which all render the same Nav and Footer), clicking 'Features' navigates to `/#features` which forces a homepage load and scroll — a jarring UX. Worse, on /contact, /help, /status, /security, /cookies the anchors would still work (they go to /#features) but lose the user's place entirely.
issues.fix: Use Next.js <Link> with scroll={false} and a manual scrollIntoView when on the homepage, or render plain '/' for non-home pages and the anchor only on home. Alternatively, accept the cross-page navigation but ensure the target sections exist.
